body:
### Summary

I would like uv to follow the [UAPI.6 Configuration Files Specification](https://uapi-group.org/specifications/specs/configuration_files_specification/) to make configuration easier to manage. I especially like that it supports having separate packager configuration under `/usr` and administrator configuration under `/etc`. Drop-ins would also be useful because it would allow extending packaged configuration instead of overriding it.

uv's current logic, as is described in [Configuration files](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/configuration-files/), seems to mostly be defined around the [XDG Base Directory Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir/0.8/). My proposal would be to keep following the user-level configuration defined there and only use UAPI.6 for system-level configuration, so I wouldn't expect anything to break unless someone is already declaring extra `uv.toml` files under `/usr` and `/etc`.

The specification is increasingly being adopted by software outside of systemd. For example, Podman recently added support to make their configuration less confusing: [Podman 6 Configuration File Changes](https://blog.podman.io/2026/06/podman-6-configuration-file-changes/). I can't find a complete list of software that supports the spec, but [Tracking upstream projects that do not support hermetic-usr for configuration](https://github.com/uapi-group/specifications/issues/76) has some relevant discussion about adoption.

### Example

[Fedora's uv package](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/uv/uv/) currently includes configuration as `/etc/uv/uv.toml`. I can override this at the user level with `~/.config/uv/uv.toml`, but it'd be useful to override this at the system level without needing to directly modify a packaged file.
title: Follow UAPI.6 Configuration Files Specification on Linux
